judgments.why: The guide states that standard OAuth apps do not require an upfront provider review process to function and can be connected immediately.
The guide explicitly mentions that you can enter up to 10 callback URLs.
The guide states that if you provide a redirect_uri that doesn't match, GitHub redirects with an error description containing redirect_uri_mismatch.
The guide states that all authenticated requests count towards your personal rate limit of 5,000 requests per hour.
The guide mentions OAuth apps and Composio-managed apps, but does not state a recommendation of GitHub Apps over OAuth apps.
The guide does not mention Public Distribution for installing the app outside your own workspace.
The guide states that the redirect_uri must use HTTPS.
The guide does not mention Non-Marketplace commercially distributed apps created after May 29, 2025 having conversations.history limited to 1 request per minute.
The guide does not mention that Slack Marketplace functional review can take up to 10 weeks.
The guide does not mention that Marketplace submission requires the app to be installed on at least 10 active workspaces.
The guide does not state the 100 test user limit for Apps in Testing status.
The guide does not mention that test-user authorizations and refresh tokens expire after seven days in Testing mode.
The guide mentions third-party security assessment fees and server storage requirements, but does not specify that it must be an annual assessment.
The guide states 'production 7-30 days', which aligns with restricted scope verification taking several weeks.
The guide does not mention brand verification or that it takes 2-3 business days.
The guide explicitly lists https://mail.google.com/ and https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.readonly as restricted scopes.
The guide states that newly created apps begin in Development Mode by default and that development mode is capped at 5 allowlisted users.
The guide states that each Spotify user using a development mode app must be added to the app allowlist under Settings -> Users Management tab.
The guide states that the app owner must maintain an active Spotify Premium subscription for development mode apps to function.
The guide mentions established business organizations and company emails, but does not state the rule about individuals vs organizations specifically as of May 15, 2025 in the context of this fact.
The guide states that quota extension applicants must maintain a minimum of 250,000 active users (250k MAUs).
The guide states that redirect URIs must use HTTPS unless using a loopback IP literal, that localhost is strictly forbidden, and to use explicit IP literals like 127.0.0.1.
The guide states: Beginning November 2020, if risk-based step-up consent is enabled, users can't consent to most newly registered multitenant apps that aren't publisher verified.
The guide states: A Partner One ID associated with a verified Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program account is required for publishing and publisher verification.
The guide states: Redirect URIs must begin with the scheme https, with exceptions for some localhost redirect URIs.
The guide states: Redirect URIs are case-sensitive and must match the case of the URL path of your running application.
The guide does not address tenant admins restricting user consent specifically based on verified publishers requiring admin consent for customers.
The guide states that apps default to the Starter tier with a cap of 5 connections.
The guide states the Core tier supports up to 50 connections.
The guide does not mention any requirements regarding listing on the Xero App Store requiring the Plus tier or above.
The guide explicitly states Free Starter tier and $35 AUD/month Core tier.
The guide mentions security assessment and use case approval for the Advanced tier, but does not address general higher tier app certification requirements.
The guide states: 'Cost Pay-per-use credit system with no monthly fees or subscriptions' and 'The X API uses pay-per-usage pricing with no subscriptions.'
The guide mentions funding developer credits via pay-per-use pricing and saving a payment card, but does not explicitly state that you buy credits upfront and they are deducted per request.
The guide mentions that read/write actions consume credits dynamically, but does not state that different endpoints have different costs.

The guide states: Apps that request advanced access for permissions and apps that allow other Businesses to access their own data must be connected to a Business that has completed Business Verification.
The guide states: The revised qualification threshold for Full Access to the Marketing API has been reduced from 1,500 to 500 Marketing API calls in the past 15 days.
The guide mentions Full Access and development tier for Marketing API, but does not state the renaming details from Standard Access to Limited Access and Advanced Access to Full Access.

notes: The live agent runs with open discovery (no curated source list), so this measures what a developer gets for an app outside the library.
Judge: a second model (verifier role) compares the generated guide to each reference fact. Spot-check eval/results.json → perApp[].judgments.
Ground-truth facts are sourced with verbatim quotes and re-verified by script; human confirmation pending.
